title: M/S Pal News Media Pvt. Ltd. And Another v. State of U.P. And 4 Others
coram: Krishna Murari, J.; Ajay Bhanot, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of at admission; licensee to consider the fresh-connection application in accordance with law and process it expeditiously in light of Seema Mansoor within 10 days of certified copy; later review/recall dismissed for want of prosecution
headnote: Where a lessee's application for a fresh electricity connection is not sanctioned solely for want of the landlord's consent, after the landlord procured permanent disconnection of the existing supply during a pending eviction suit, the writ court will not itself grant the connection. Following Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd., Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides either the owner's consent or, in its absence, an indemnity bond by the occupier; a licensee cannot refuse supply to a tenant, lessee or occupier merely for want of the landlord's consent. Recording the licensee's statement that the fresh-connection application would be processed expeditiously in that light, the Court directed the licensee to consider the application in accordance with law and process it expeditiously in light of Seema Mansoor within ten days of production of a certified copy. A later review/recall application was dismissed for want of prosecution.
facts:
M/S Pal News Media Pvt. Ltd. and another took a lease of premise No. B-175, Sector-44, Noida, District Gautam Budh Nagar, from the fifth respondent on 19 January 2017. The landlord then filed a suit for eviction, still pending before the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Gautam Budh Nagar, and applied to the distribution licensee (respondents 3 and 4) for permanent disconnection. The connection was permanently disconnected on 26 December 2017.

The petitioners applied on 2 January 2018 to transfer the connection into their name and were told it could not be transferred without the landlord's consent. They applied again on 9 January 2018 for a fresh connection at the same premises. Their grievance was that even that application was not being sanctioned for want of the landlord's consent. With the parties' consent the writ was finally disposed of at admission without a counter-affidavit.

holding_units.clause: 4.4 and Annexure 4.2 — occupier/lessee; owner's consent or indemnity bond
holding_units.topic: lessee/occupier cannot be refused a fresh connection solely for want of the landlord's consent; application to be considered in light of Seema Mansoor
holding_units.question: May a licensee refuse a lessee's application for a fresh electricity connection solely because the landlord, who procured disconnection amid a pending eviction, withholds consent?
holding_units.holding: Following Seema Mansoor, no. Clause 4.4 of the Code, as construed in that decision, provides either a consent letter of the owner or, in its absence, an indemnity bond by the lessee, tenant or occupier. Every owner or occupier, including a tenant, has a statutory right to apply and obtain supply subject to the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Code; an application cannot be refused merely for want of the landlord's consent. The Court did not itself grant the connection. Recording counsel's statement that the petitioners' fresh-connection application would be processed expeditiously in light of Seema Mansoor, it directed respondents 2, 3 and 4 to consider that application in accordance with law and process it expeditiously in light of Seema Mansoor within ten days of production of a certified copy.
holding_units.qualifier: The operative direction is confined to the 9.1.2018 fresh-connection application. Transfer of the disconnected connection, the pending eviction, and occupancy on the merits were not decided.

principle_tags.application: The Court adopted Seema Mansoor's reading of Clause 4.4: the Code provides either the owner's consent or an occupier's indemnity bond, so a lessee/tenant cannot be refused supply merely for want of the landlord's consent.

principle_tags.application: The adopted Seema Mansoor extract treats Annexure 4.2 as the occupier's indemnity path where the owner's consent is not obtained, and holds that a proper application with that indemnity cannot be refused solely for want of landlord consent.

principle_tags.application: The petitioners were told even a fresh connection would not be sanctioned without the landlord's consent. Following Seema Mansoor, that is not a lawful ground of refusal.

authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd., Lucknow and others
authorities.proposition: Clause 4.4 of the Supply Code provides either the owner's consent or an occupier's indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2); every owner or occupier, including a tenant, has a statutory right to apply and obtain supply subject to the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Code, and the licensee cannot refuse a connection solely for want of the landlord's consent.
